surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between TMGa and surface arsenic atoms followed by dissociation into GaCH3 and release of two CH3 radicals. The desorption of CH3 from GaCH3 results in the formation of gallium atoms, which tend to form Ga-Ga dimer bonds. The two released CH3 radicals can be attached to either surface As or Ga atoms. Attachment of CH3 radicals to nearby arsenic atoms hinders further reactions between these arsenic atoms and impinging TMGa molecules. The desorption of CH3 radicals from arsenic atoms allows these arsenic atoms to become active again toward TMGa dissociation.
evidence: A recent study by Memmert and Yu shows that TMGa reacts with surface arsenic atoms and dissociates into GaCH3, releasing two CH3 radicals on the surface. These methyl radicals desorb in two channels: one for the desorption of CH3 from GaCH3, the other for the desorption of CH3 from the GaAs(001) surface. Desorption of CH3 from the adsorbed GaCH3, as described previously, results in the formation of gallium atoms, which tend to form Ga-Ga dimer bonds as judged by the increasing RD signal. On the other hand, the two released CH3 radicals associated with TMGa dissociation could be attached to either surface As or Ga atoms.
